cluster.bound_formula: (nodes - 1) x ceil(per_node_reservation_rate x broadcast_interval_ms / 1000), from architecture-map.md section 3: the overshoot is what the other nodes admitted within one broadcast_interval, and inside that window a node admits everything it attempts

database.server_version: PostgreSQL 16.13 (Debian 16.13-1.pgdg13+1) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

label: cluster_2
notes: package.git_dirty is null: answering it needs git, which this library never runs (decision D11). scripts/v1/bench.sh sets AURORA_BENCH_GIT_DIRTY.

every node reserves against one shared key with a hard limit of 10000. The overshoot is the admissions above that limit, and the bound it is asserted against is computed from the configured broadcast_interval and the measured per-node rate, not from a constant.
cluster_2 ran on 2 real BEAM nodes started with :peer, each with its own supervision tree and connection pool against one database and one distributed PubSub. This is not a simulation.

the whole burst finished in 20.1 percent of one broadcast_interval, so NO gossip tick occurred during it and every node admitted up to the hard limit independently. That is the worst case the guarantee allows and not a steady-state figure; admitted_after_one_settling_window is what shows convergence.
persisted total after a flush on every node: 20000 (expected 20000)

latency_us.p50, p95, p99 and max are null: this mode took no per-operation timing sample. Its unit of work is not an operation in a loop, so a percentile over operations would be a number with no referent.
